title: Review native-pr-landing design and fold in squash-trailer evidence
summary: Write an independent review of docs/design/native-pr-landing.md (no review file exists; the earlier attempt was rejected) and revise the design to address its findings. The revision records today's GitHub evidence: squash appends a Co-authored-by paragraph that buries Athena-Job trailers, and one squash may name only one landed job. It also states that this design precedes the parallel pool, per parallel-jobs F1.

defaults_applied.how: Review and design claims cite files and lines, and the new GitHub behavior is labeled as observed on 2026-10-13 rather than reproduced.
The design is reviewed independently before any build; alternatives stay recorded.
The review is written to be read without context.
Review plus one design revision; other files are touched only for consistency.
No personal data or secrets in the text.
A verifier checks each criterion against the diff and runs the cargo checks.

assumptions: No review file for native-pr-landing exists in the repository; the rejected first review left nothing to build on, so this one is written from scratch as review-1.
'Independently' means the reviewer judges the design against the repository and the brief without relying on the author's claims, then the design is revised to match.
'RM-0' is the roadmap item for native PR landing; I read this as a design-review task, not implementation.
The Co-authored-by and one-job-per-squash facts come from the user's evidence today and can be cited as such; the producer cannot re-run GitHub.
parallel-jobs-review-1.md F1 is the finding that this design must precede the parallel pool; the producer will read it to cite it exactly.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new review file under docs/design/reviews/ for native-pr-landing lists numbered findings, each citing the section or line of the design it concerns and a severity, and ends with a verdict.

The design states how Athena-Job trailers are found when GitHub's squash appends a Co-authored-by paragraph after them: trailers are no longer the last paragraph, so the design either reads the host's merged commit via the client or sets the squash message itself. It labels the evidence as observed on 2026-10-13 and says how it was observed.

The design states that one squash commit can name only one landed job. It states what follows for the chain rule (M30) and for a pull request that holds several jobs: one job per pull request, or an explicit rule for the others.

The design says it must be settled before the parallel pool and links the F1 finding in docs/design/reviews/parallel-jobs-review-1.md. Any cross-reference edit in parallel-jobs.md is consistent with it.
Each review finding is either resolved in the revised design or listed as an open question, and the Status line reflects the review outcome.
Claims keep the (read)/(design) labels. New numbers or observations are cited or marked as estimates. No secrets or personal data, including email addresses, appear in the text.
No Rust code, governance file or records/ path changes; only Markdown files change.

Run `git status` and `git diff --stat`: only .md files are changed or added. Run `cargo test` and `cargo clippy`: they still pass, because any docs-consistency tests, such as the M24 named-test check or the requirements-map checks, accept the edits.

out_of_scope: Implementing athena land --pr or any code
Changing the squash-chain rule's implementation (M30) or enforcement tests
Reviewing or revising the parallel-jobs design beyond a cross-reference
departures: Slightly higher p50 and a lower verification pass rate than the reference: design-review output is judged subjectively, and the work depends on reading several long docs (squash-chain-landing, parallel-jobs and its review).
